name: OK-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+23 partisan lean in rural Oklahoma
Frank Lucas's long incumbency and roughly 55-to-1 fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price Lucas near 96% to win
No public polling and minimal Democratic investment in the race
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Lucas: a Republican-leaning district, a decades-long incumbent, and a fundraising gap of more than $1 million to about $18,000. Markets agree, pricing the Democrat at roughly 2%, and no polling or ratings suggest any competitive opening for Byrd.
model.watch: Only a major scandal involving Lucas combined with a large national Democratic wave could put this seat in play, and even then the district's lean would make an upset difficult.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Frank Lucas seeks another term in a western Oklahoma district that leans Republican by about 23 points. He has represented the area since the 1990s and enters the general election with more than $570,000 on hand after raising over $1 million. Suzie Byrd has raised under $20,000, leaving her with little capacity to introduce herself to voters or advertise.

No public polls cover the race, and no national ratings have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets give Lucas roughly a 96% chance of winning, consistent with the district's fundamentals. The forecast expects Lucas to win by about 20 points, with the main uncertainty being turnout patterns in a low-attention race rather than any genuine competitive threat.
